long_session.note: 60 s of live game runtime with every target patched in 39 modules, checked alive every 5 s
long_session.meaning: The shim was live 35 ms after install and stayed live for a minute; the game made no file open through any patched slot in that time. Asset reads therefore do not use these entry points at all in this build.

interaction_run.note: Game window activated with xdotool and sent space/Return to leave the idle screen, 20 s of runtime after input
interaction_run.meaning: Driving input in this environment does not produce asset I/O through any patched slot either, so the asset path cannot be reached by this method and no in-game redirect can be demonstrated yet.

attempts.what: WINAPI CreateFileW shim patched into every module's import slot
attempts.why: In the Wine stand-in, a second module (wprobe.dll) calling through its patched KERNEL32!CreateFileW slot terminated the process with no crash record and no file-log entry. The shim is therefore unproven and possibly unsafe, so the target and its probe harness were deleted rather than shipped.
attempts.in_game: It did patch 14 modules in the real game without breaking start-up, but was never observed being called there either.

conclusion: All four targets (CreateFileA, fopen, fopen_s, _wfopen) are patched in 39 loaded modules of the real game, and the shim is proven live in-process: it captured a CreateFileA open of \\.\pipe\wine_plugplay. No asset open was observed in 22-35 s of game time, so HYPER DEMON's asset reads do not use any of these import slots. hyperdemon.exe imports only CreateFileA/ReadFile from KERNEL32 and fopen/fopen_s/_wfopen from the UCRT API set, so the remaining candidates are the kernelbase/NtCreateFile path (no import slot to patch) or the Steam API file layer. No in-game asset replacement has been achieved yet.
